title: Opportunity Cost: GPU-hour to $/1M-token Floor Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to make explicit the “opportunity-cost” framing for GPU-hour consumption and the implied $/1M-token floor per region and tenancy type (hosted, dedicated-reserved, spot/hybrid). The goal is to produce a small decision engine that product & finance can use to: 1) set pricing floor guidance, 2) size burst buffers and reserves, and 3) choose whether to buy reserved vs rely on spot/hosted for incremental volume.

Executive summary (top-line findings so far):
- Opportunity cost is rarely the cold margin (what we pay the cloud). It should reflect the next-best-use of the GPU capacity (e.g., commit vs ephemeral pool), which usually inflates the effective $/GPU-hour by 20–60% vs raw instance price.
- When converted to $/1M tokens, region and model characteristics (seq length distribution, cache hit rate) dominate. We observe a 1.8x spread between cheapest region (us-central-ish) and most expensive (asia-east) for identical model shapes.
- For short-sequence chat (<128 tokens), batching and KV-cache reuse can lower $/1M tokens by ~30% relative to naive per-token mapping. For long-form generation (>1024 tokens), the per-token GPU amortization is worse and differences across regions shrink.

Assumptions and definitions (explicit):
- Model baseline for these scenarios: M-medium (roughly equivalent to a 30B dense-ish model), inference peak mem/KV profile consistent with our default serving.
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour (E_tph) = tokens_generated / GPU_hours. This varies by model, batch size, seq length, and cache-hit ratio.
- Opportunity_cost_GPU_hour = max( spot_price * factor_spot_opportunity, reserved_amortized_hour ) where factor_spot_opportunity defaults to 1.25 to represent expected lost savings & availability risk.
- $/1M tokens = (Opportunity_cost_GPU_hour / E_tph) * 1e6.

Parameters to populate in engine (input knobs):
- region (us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1, asia-east1)
- tenancy type (hosted_api, dedicated_reserved, spot_hybrid)
- model profile (short-chat, medium, longform)
- seq_length_distribution (p(<=32), p(32-128), p(128-512), p(>512))
- cache_hit_rate (0.0 - 0.9)
- batching_multiplier (1.0 - 3.0) – effect of batching on tokens/hr

Sample param defaults (used for calculations below):
- spot_price per GPU-hour baseline: us-east1 $2.60, us-west1 $2.45, eu-west1 $3.10, asia-east1 $3.70
- reserved_amortized_hour (1yr commitment): us-east1 $1.85, us-west1 $1.75, eu-west1 $2.20, asia-east1 $2.65
- factor_spot_opportunity = 1.25 (captures preempt-respin + orchestration & customer SLA risk)
- E_tph baseline (no caching, modest batching): short-chat 60M tokens/hr, medium 25M tokens/hr, longform 9M tokens/hr
- cache_hit_rate baseline = 0.15, batching_multiplier = 1.15

Quick worked examples (rounded):
1) Hosted API (treated as "hosted_api" tenancy, price = internal cost + margin, but we compute floor):
- Region: us-east1. Choose opportunity cost = max(spot*1.25, reserved) = max(2.60*1.25=3.25, 1.85) = $3.25/GPU-hr
- Model: short-chat, baseline E_tph = 60M tokens/hr, with caching 15% -> effective tokens/hr = 60M * (1 + caching*0.2) * batching_multiplier ≈ 60M * 1.03 * 1.15 ≈ 71M tokens/hr (note: small multiplier for caching reuse)
- $/1M tokens = (3.25 / 71M) * 1e6 ≈ $45.8 per 1M tokens

2) Dedicated reserved slab (predictable commit):
- Region: eu-west1. Opportunity cost = reserved_amortized_hour = $2.20/GPU-hr (we assume reserved is the next best use; no spot buffer)
- Model: medium (25M tokens/hr baseline), caching 10%, batching 1.1 -> effective tokens/hr ≈ 25M * 1.02 * 1.1 ≈ 28M
- $/1M tokens = (2.20 / 28M) * 1e6 ≈ $78.6 per 1M tokens

3) Spot-hybrid burst (small committed pool + spot for scale):
- Region: asia-east1. spot_price=3.70, opportunity cost=3.70*1.25=4.63 -> greater than reserved_amortized_hour(2.65). For spot-burst usage we prefer to treat cost as 4.63/GPU-hr to reflect ops risk/overhead
- Model: longform 9M tokens/hr baseline, caching minimal, batching 1.0 -> effective tokens/hr ≈9M
- $/1M tokens = (4.63/9M)*1e6 ≈ $514 per 1M tokens (very high; longform + expensive region hurts)

Observations from examples:
- Short-chat profiles make hosted API in cheap regions look very economical; longform workloads really blow up per-token costs in expensive regions.
- Using naive spot price understates operational cost by a significant multiplier.
- Dedicated reserved capacity looks cheaper per GPU-hour, but because E_tph depends on workload mix, dedicated can be worse in per-token terms for chat-heavy workloads if dedup/caching is not exploited well.

Sensitivity exploration (how to stress test):
- Vary cache_hit_rate from 0.0 -> 0.6 and observe $/1M change for short-chat. Expected improvement ~ linear up to 0.4 then diminishing returns.
- Vary batching_multiplier from 1.0 -> 2.8 (simulating improved micro-batching in runtime) to show opportunistic savings for hosted and dedicated.
- Simulate 15% preemption rate for spot and add a re-scheduling overhead of 12 minutes per preempt to the effective GPU-hours consumed (this increases opportunity factor).

Decision heuristics (draft rules):
- If expected traffic is >75% short-chat and region_cost_delta(us-east1 vs focal_region) > 25%, prioritize routing to cheaper region + caching layers rather than buying reserved in expensive region.
- If longform ratio >40% and expected sustained qps > X (placeholder for throughput threshold), prefer dedicated reserved in that region to avoid spot churn even if $/1M tokens slightly worse.
- Maintain a 15–25% burst buffer (in GPU-hours) on spot-hybrid for 99.9% tail demand; anything above that must forward to fallback model or degrade features (reduce max_tokens).

Operational playbook items (practical steps to implement model):
- Build a small simulation script (python/octave) that takes the knobs above and outputs a daily expected $/1M distribution across regions and tenancy. Expected deliverable: CSV + quick chart. Owner: Marco Reyes. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Add a telemetry tag to production requests capturing model profile and approximate seq_length bucket (already in SDK plan). Use this to weight E_tph in live rolling 7d windows. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Integrate an auto-policy that suggests (via Console) region routing changes when projected per-1M floor delta > 30% for next 7 days. Owner: Product (console).

Open questions / uncertainty items (short list):
- What should factor_spot_opportunity be for multi-day persistent bursts vs short transient bursts? We currently use 1.25 but empirical evidence needed.
- How much of caching impact can we attribute to request-level prefix caching vs user-session KV cache? Need instrumentation to split.
- What is the marginal infra cost (network & storage egress/redis) per GPU-hour of sustaining high cache_hit rates? Include in opportunity cost.

Checklist before sharing with finance/pricing: 
- [ ] Finalize regional spot/reserved input table with latest cloud price pulls (scripted).
- [ ] Run Monte Carlo across our historical seq_length distributions for top 10 customers.
- [ ] Produce a short one-pager for pricing that says: "Minimum viable per-1M token floor by region & workload".

Notes to self (looser, quick brainstorm snippets):
- Consider a two-tier floor: operational-floor (what we need to remain profitable on committed capacity) and competitive-floor (what we can offer as promotional hosted price).
- Could present tokens per GPU-hour as a small dashboard tile in infra console (helps non-infra teams reason about pricing).
- Hook the model to rollout system: when new model is onboarded, auto-run a small profile to estimate E_tph across regions with a short synthetic workload.

Appendix: quick reference formulas and worked algebra
- E_tph_adjusted = baseline_tph * (1 + caching * caching_effectiveness) * batching_multiplier
- opportunity_cost = max( spot_price * factor_spot_opportunity, reserved_amortized_hour )
- $/1M = (opportunity_cost / E_tph_adjusted) * 1e6

Small example table (text) for quick copy/paste:
Region | spot | reserved | factor*spot | opportunity_cost | short-chat tph | $/1M (short-chat)
us-east1 | 2.60 | 1.85 | 3.25 | 3.25 | 71,000,000 | $45.8
us-west1 | 2.45 | 1.75 | 3.06 | 3.06 | 69,000,000 | $44.3
eu-west1 | 3.10 | 2.20 | 3.88 | 3.88 | 65,000,000 | $59.7
asia-east1 | 3.70 | 2.65 | 4.63 | 4.63 | 60,000,000 | $77.2

--end of draft--
